why: Defines the pricing contract using team standard: dollars, fractions, None for not found.

value: tax.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct=0) -> tax.TaxResult. lines: list of (category: str, amount_cents: int) per invoice line, amounts BEFORE customer discount (invoice.py/pricing.py supply them). region: customer region code like "TX", or None for an unknown customer (0% tax, no error). discount_pct: customer discount percent (0 if none). TaxResult fields (all cents ints except pcts): tax_cents, rate_pct, discount_pct, taxable_subtotal_cents, exempt_subtotal_cents, taxable_base_cents (Decimal, may be fractional cents). Unknown region string -> KeyError. Also tax.get_tax_pct(region)->float and tax.is_exempt(category)->bool. Categories and regions matched case-insensitively after strip().
why: agent2 owns tax; invoice.py must call compute_tax instead of computing tax itself. Proposes the signature so pricing (agent1) knows to pass per-line (category, cents) and customer region/discount, and invoice (agent3) knows what fields TaxResult has. Unknown customer = region None, not an exception, per RULES.md.

agent3 reviewed: compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) returning TaxResult works for invoice. Invoice will convert between cents and Decimal dollars at the boundary. Invoice passes lines BEFORE discount and region None for unknown customers.

agent1 (pricing): our team standard is money as float dollars and percentages as fractions (10% = 0.10). pricing_api returns unit_price in dollars and discount_rate as a fraction. Please align tax_api: compute_tax(lines, region, discount_rate=0.0) where lines = list of (category, amount_dollars float) BEFORE discount; region None = unknown customer -> 0 tax; unknown region -> KeyError; returns object with tax_amount (float dollars), rate (float fraction), taxable_base (float dollars). Keep the rest of your semantics (case-insensitive region/category, is_exempt, get_tax_pct as fraction). If you need cents internally, convert at your boundary.
superseded by v2 adapting to pricing_api units (dollars and fractions), per agent1 objection

value: tax.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_rate=0) -> tax.TaxResult. Units follow pricing_api: money in dollars (float/Decimal, rounded to cents by tax), discounts and rates as fractions. lines: list of (category: str, amount_dollars) per invoice line, amounts BEFORE customer discount (amount = unit_price * qty). region: customer region code (e.g. "TX") from get_customer(...)["region"], or None for an unknown customer (0% tax, no error). discount_rate: customer discount_rate fraction (0.10 = 10% off), 0 if none. Returns TaxResult with: tax (dollars, rounded half up to the cent), rate (fraction, e.g. 0.0825 for TX), discount_rate (fraction applied), taxable_subtotal (dollars before discount, non-exempt lines), exempt_subtotal (dollars). Unknown region string -> KeyError. Also tax.get_tax_rate(region)->float fraction, tax.is_exempt(category)->bool. Categories and regions are matched case-insensitively after strip(). Internally tax.py computes in integer cents with Decimal.
why: v2 adapts to pricing_api units (dollars and fractions) that agent1 objected to v1 over; agent1 said they accept dollars/fractions. Tax still owns taxability, base and rounding; it does not look up items or customers itself. Team cents/percent convention is kept only inside tax.py. Unknown customer = region None -> 0% tax (RULES.md).

agent3 accepts tax_api v2: dollars, fractions, region None for unknown customer, TaxResult.tax and .rate as specified. Invoice will use tax.tax (dollars) and tax.rate (fraction) and convert to Decimal at the boundary.
agent2: region and category fields are what tax needs; get_customer region/discount_rate fraction and get_item category match tax_api v2.
agent1 accepts tax_api v2: dollars and fractions, region from get_customer, None for unknown customer.
